claims: "Integrity" is the official name given by the Artemis II crew to their Orion spacecraft.
"Integrity" represents trust, respect, candor, and humility, as well as the integrated efforts of NASA and the Canadian Space Agency.
The Artemis II crew successfully piloted Integrity around the Moon and back.
Integrity had a safe splashdown in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.
Integrity is the first crewed Orion spacecraft.
Integrity marks the first human mission beyond low Earth orbit since 1972.
Astronauts manually flew Integrity to test its capabilities.
Astronauts performed manual maneuvering to align Integrity for power generation during the 10-day mission.
The Artemis II mission lasted 10 days.
The name "Integrity" was chosen to represent the core values and dedication of the thousands of people involved in the Artemis program.
Integrity successfully handled the high-heat reentry.
Parachutes deployed in sequence on Integrity to land in the Pacific Ocean.
Navy teams awaited in the Pacific Ocean.
Integrity was officially named during a September 2025 news conference.
